name_note: GTDB g__Lactobacillus follows the 2020 emended, narrow genus; many species in older papers now belong to other genera such as Lactiplantibacillus or Limosilactobacillus.

sentences.text: Lactobacillus is a genus of lactic acid bacteria; in 2020 the broad genus of 261 species was split into 25 genera, leaving an emended, host-adapted Lactobacillus.
Members ferment sugars to lactic acid; the dairy starter Lactobacillus delbrueckii is noted for efficient lactose use and rapid acidification.
The genus is long recognised for roles in food fermentation and as a mainstay of probiotic preparations.
In the female genital tract, protective Lactobacillus strains dominate a balanced vaginal microecology.
Reviews have associated depletion of lactobacilli, with overgrowth of anaerobes, with persistence of high-risk papillomavirus infection and cervical malignant transformation.
